analysis.investment_thesis: Parmeshwar Metal is a tiny copper scrap recycler with a pitiful 0.20% ROE — this is not a business, it's a commodity trading operation with near-zero returns on capital. At INR 189 Cr market cap with these return metrics, there is nothing here that resembles a compounder.
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 72.03% — skin in the game
P/E of 12x is not demanding in absolute terms
Recycling theme has structural tailwinds long-term
key_risks: ROE of 0.20% is catastrophically low — capital destruction territory
Commodity business (copper) with zero pricing power or brand moat
Young company (incorporated 2016), no track record through a full cycle
red_flags: ROE 0.20% versus my 15%+ minimum threshold — disqualifying
Virtually no institutional holding (DII 0.03%, FII 0%) signals lack of scrutiny
P/E of 12x on near-zero earnings is mathematically meaningless
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I invest in businesses I can understand that generate consistent, high returns on capital — DMart earns 15%+ ROE because customers come back every week for groceries. Parmeshwar Metal earns 0.20% ROE recycling copper scrap into wire; it is a pure commodity conversion business with no moat, no brand, and no customer stickiness. Copper prices swing, scrap availability swings, and margins are razor-thin. A P/E of 12 looks cheap until you realize the 'E' is almost nothing — this is optically cheap, fundamentally expensive.

The promoter holding at 72% is the only redeeming feature, but promoter quality means nothing if the underlying business cannot generate returns above the cost of capital. I have no visibility into debt levels, working capital cycles (critical in scrap businesses), or cash flow quality from this snapshot, but the 0.20% ROE alone tells me capital is being destroyed or barely preserved. This fails my first filter. Pass — permanently — and look elsewhere.
